strings.name: Geoffrey Hinton
strings.summary: Geoffrey Hinton advanced backpropagation, representation learning and visual recognition with collaborators. He built a research group in Toronto and shared Turing and Nobel prizes. After leaving Google, he focused more on advanced-AI risks; his forecasts are research judgments, not completed events.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2026, not an exhaustive news record. Institutional achievements are team efforts; announced plans are not completed results.
strings.influence.rationale: Made foundational contributions to neural networks and deep learning and advanced public discussion of AI risks.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Cambridge psychology, 1970; Edinburgh PhD in artificial intelligence, 1978
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Deep-learning foundations
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Worked with colleagues and students on neural-network training and visual-recognition breakthroughs.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Recognition and public debate
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Shared the Turing and Nobel Physics prizes and advocated serious research into AI safety.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Vienna Gödel Lecture
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Spoke at TU Wien about AI capabilities, control and safety.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Shared the prize with John Hopfield for foundations of machine learning with neural networks.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Left Google
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Ended his Google work and expanded public discussion of AI risks.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Shared the 2018 award with Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: AlexNet breakthrough
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Collaborated with Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever on influential image-recognition work.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Joined Toronto
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Began long-term research and student supervision at the University of Toronto.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Backpropagation research
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Published influential multilayer-network training research with David Rumelhart and Ronald Williams.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Earned a doctorate
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Completed a PhD in artificial intelligence at Edinburgh.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Cambridge graduation
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Completed undergraduate study in experimental psychology.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Wimbledon
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in the London area of the United Kingdom.
